Previous reports suggested Apple planned to launch a 20th anniversary edition iPhone next year, featuring an all-glass body design. However, analysts at investment bank Jefferies believe that device is no longer moving forward.

Wall Street analysts say the ambitious redesign plans for the 20th anniversary iPhone have been scrapped.

Wall Street investment bank Jefferies downgraded Apple's stock rating to "Underperform" today, with analyst Edison Lee pointing out that the potential cancellation of the 20th anniversary iPhone redesign is one of the main reasons for the downgrade.

The key to this downgrade lies in reports that Apple's all-glass iPhone project has been cancelled. Although rumours about the project being in development surfaced as early as 2025, with some expecting a 2027 launch, Apple has never responded to such speculation. However, Apple quietly filed a patent for an "all-glass enclosure" back in 2019. Jefferies previously considered an all-glass iPhone reasonable and credible, but Edison Lee believes development has stalled. The analyst noted that supply chain checks indicate the project was terminated due to poor yield rates. Edison Lee believes that, with memory costs soaring, this decision is a "significant blow" to driving high-end iPhone sales. He estimated that if the device had launched on schedule in September 2027 to celebrate the iPhone's 20th anniversary, its average retail price would have reached US$2,060, higher than the average selling price of any previous model. Edison Lee wrote: "More importantly, we believe Apple originally planned to extend the all-glass design to future iPhone Pro and Pro Max models, thereby further increasing the average selling price and gross margin." He believes that, with memory prices rising, this should have been an important defensive strategy.

Edison Lee also pointed out that Apple's artificial intelligence strategy and rising component costs for the iPhone 19 Pro are other reasons for the stock downgrade.

According to Edison Lee's report, it is not entirely clear whether the analyst believes the entire redesign plan has been completely shelved, or only some design elements have been abandoned.

The most upvoted comment was posted by Currentinterest.

These analysts have been wrong too many times about Apple's future plans. Even the term "all-glass" never accurately reflected Apple's true intentions. The 20th anniversary phone will be unique and creative, and whatever the final design, it will sell like hotcakes.

For example, there have been rumours for months that Apple will not be able to completely remove the Dynamic Island cutout next year. Therefore, an all-glass screen is simply not possible. However, the rumoured quad-curved edge design could still happen.

In any case, if the design of the iPhone 20th anniversary edition has indeed been cancelled, credible media outlets should soon confirm it.
